claim_tested: Host-side wall-clock elapsed time, anchored at a fixed action (PCSX.hardResetEmulator() + PCSX.resumeEmulator() via the Lua console), is a reliable proxy for movie/boot-sequence playback position.
method: Two independent runs, each: reset+resume via Lua, then screenshot every 2.0s for 40.0s, each sample hashed (SHA-256 of raw pixel bytes). Compared samples at matching t-indices across the two runs.

result.pattern: All 12 samples from t=0.00s through t=22.77s matched byte-for-byte across both runs. From t=24.82s onward (into what is plausibly the opening movie/cinematic, given the earlier Stage 4 boot timeline), most samples still matched (13, 14, 16, 18, 19) but 3 of 8 did not.

interpretation: The early boot sequence (BIOS/logos, roughly the first 23 seconds) is fully deterministic against wall-clock time -- rebooting twice and sampling at the same offsets reproduces byte-identical frames every time. Once into the region with rapidly-changing content (plausibly real movie playback), most samples still matched but a minority did not, at a fixed 2-second sampling interval. This is most likely explained by ordinary host-side timing jitter (HTTP round-trip variance for each screenshot request) becoming significant once the underlying content changes frame-to-frame -- a few hundred milliseconds of jitter can land on an adjacent, different frame when content changes every frame, but not when the same static image persists for seconds at a time. This has not been proven to be jitter rather than genuine non-determinism in the game's own playback -- that distinction was not isolated in this pass (e.g. by sampling at a much finer interval, or by measuring the actual host-side round-trip time per screenshot to correlate mismatches with slow requests).
relevance_to_stage_5: For SDD O5 (external, host-side subtitle sync), this is an encouraging partial result: subtitle cues typically span multiple seconds, so occasional few-hundred-millisecond drift during fast-changing content is unlikely to be perceptible, and the mechanism is exact during slower-paced content. It does NOT establish a frame-exact PS1-side timing source, which is what SDD O6 (internal/native movie subtitle composition) would need -- that remains unproven and would still require either finer-grained determinism testing or genuine in-RAM instrumentation of the movie-player executable family.
caveats: Only one boot path was tested (fresh hardResetEmulator + resumeEmulator from an already-loaded disc), not a full cold power-on through the disc-loading dialog.

Sampling interval was 2.0s -- coarse relative to a 60fps/16.7ms frame. The mismatches found do not distinguish 'off by one frame due to host jitter' from 'the game's own playback timing varies run to run' -- both remain possible explanations.
Not yet tested: whether the specific frames that mismatched are visually similar (adjacent frames of the same scene) or wildly different (which would suggest something other than simple jitter).
